text:
The unemployment rate was 6.3% with a fed funds rate of 0.10%, which points to mid-2014. Equities were up 24% over 12 months, which fits the period from early 2013 to early 2014 or to mid-2014. The 10-year yield was 2.54%, having fallen 0.19 over three months, which is consistent with June 2014 (2.53%). Unemployment in June 2014 was 6.1% as first reported, but 6.3% was the May 2014 figure as first reported.

Headline CPI at 2.14% YoY fits May 2014 (2.1%), and core at 1.95% fits as well. The 3-month average payroll gain of 234k also fits spring 2014. Industrial production at +4.27% YoY fits too.

Gold rose 6.3% in one month, which fits January 2014 (+3%) or June 2014 (+6% on Iraq). The 2-year yield at 0.45% matches May–June 2014. The 10-year at 2.54% matches the end of May 2014 (2.48%) or June (2.53%). Unemployment in the data, 6.3%, is the latest published value. At the end of June, the June figure of 6.1% would have been published in early July, so the latest published value at the end of June would be the May figure of 6.3%. That points to June 2014.

Equity returns for 1 month of +2.1% match June 2014 (+2.1%). Gold up 6.3% in June also matches.
